Reliability profile of a planned allocation

Source: R/design.R
reliability_design.Rd

Computes the reliability profile of a planned allocation of individuals to sites and compares it with the balanced allocation of the same total, or with equal spending when the costs per individual differ.

Usage

reliability_design(
  n,
  sigma_tau,
  kappa = NULL,
  p = 0.5,
  R2 = 0,
  var_outcome = 1,
  cost = NULL
)

Arguments

n

Planned numbers of individuals in the sites, a numeric vector of positive numbers.

sigma_tau

Planned between-site standard deviation of the effects, a positive number, or a numeric vector of them for a range of scenarios. The printed comparison uses the first.

kappa

Optional constants \(\kappa_j\) with \(v_j = \kappa_j / n_j\), one for all sites or one per site. By default they come from p, R2 and var_outcome, as in neyman_variance().

p

Proportion of each site's individuals assigned to treatment, numbers strictly between 0 and 1, one for all sites or one per site.

R2

Proportion of the outcome variance explained by covariates, numbers in \([0, 1)\), one for all sites or one per site.

var_outcome

Variance of the outcome within each arm of a site (\(s_j^2\) in equation 2 of Lee, 2026), positive numbers, one for all sites or one per site.

cost

Optional costs per individual in each site, positive numbers. The comparison is then with equal spending of the same budget.

Value

An object of class reliability_design, a list whose main components are

  • n, kappa, se2, sigma_tau, cost: the inputs, with the sampling variances se2.

  • planned, balanced: reliability_profile objects of the planned allocation and of the balanced one (or equal spending) at the first sigma_tau.

  • balanced_n: the sizes of the balanced allocation or of equal spending.

  • efficiency: the ratio of the geometric to the arithmetic mean of the planned sizes.

  • local: the approximation of Appendix E.2, a list with the coefficient of variation of the sizes cv, the logarithm of the efficiency exact, its approximation leading (\(-\mathrm{CV}^2/2\)) and the bound on the remainder bound (NA when a size is twice the mean or more).

  • scenarios: a data frame with the informativeness of both allocations at each sigma_tau.

print(), profile_summary() (with a column allocation), site_table() (with the columns n, kappa and n_balanced), reliability_profile() (the planned profile), report_text() and plot_design() take it.

Details

With a fixed number of sites \(J\), a fixed total \(N\) and a common \(\kappa\), the balanced allocation \(n_j = N/J\) maximizes the informativeness and the mean reliability, and minimizes the benchmark risk; there \(I = \sigma_\tau^2 / (\sigma_\tau^2 + \kappa J / N)\) (Lee, 2026, Proposition 4). The informativeness depends on the sizes through their geometric mean \(\tilde n\): with \(u_j = n_j / \bar n - 1\) and \(\mathrm{CV}_J^2 = J^{-1}\sum_j u_j^2\), \(\log(\tilde n / \bar n) = -\mathrm{CV}_J^2/2 + R\) with \(|R| \le J^{-1}\sum_j |u_j|^3 / \{3(1 - r)^3\}\) when every \(|u_j| \le r < 1\) (Appendix E.2). The component local contains this approximation and its bound.

With unequal costs \(c_j\), the allocation that maximizes the informativeness for a budget \(B\) spends the same on every site, \(n_j = B / (J c_j)\) (Appendix E.3). With constants \(\kappa_j\) that differ, balance still maximizes the informativeness, because \(\mathrm{GM}(v) = \mathrm{GM}(\kappa)/\mathrm{GM}(n)\), but it need not make the reliabilities equal or maximize the mean reliability (Appendix E.3).

These results concern the site profile at known inputs: the informativeness, the mean reliability and the benchmark risk, not ranks or the distribution of the effects.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

See also

balanced_allocation() and solve_design() for allocations and sizes, and vignette("planning") for a worked plan.

Examples

n <- round(exp(qnorm(seq(0.5 / 40, 1 - 0.5 / 40, length.out = 40), 3.8, 0.47)))
design <- reliability_design(n, sigma_tau = 0.2, kappa = 4)
design
#> Planned allocation: 40 sites, 1,990 individuals, kappa = 4, sigma_tau = 0.2
#> Site sizes from 16 to 128 (CV 0.48)
#> 
#>                              planned    balanced
#>   informativeness I          0.309      0.332
#>   mean reliability           0.317      0.332
#>   dispersion H               0.0225     0.0000
#>   concentration count J_eff  36.6       40.0
#>   geometric mean size        44.7       49.8
#> 
#> Balance maximizes I and the mean reliability at fixed J and N when every site
#> has the same kappa and the same cost per individual (Lee, 2026).

# The informativeness of both allocations over a range of sigma_tau
reliability_design(n, sigma_tau = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3), kappa = 4)$scenarios
#>   sigma_tau I_planned I_balanced
#> 1       0.1 0.1006091  0.1106170
#> 2       0.2 0.3091319  0.3322204
#> 3       0.3 0.5016873  0.5281628
